priceSnapshot.note: SCHEDULING ANOMALY, STATED UP FRONT SO NOTHING BELOW IS MISREAD. This run is labelled endday because the scheduler labelled it endday, but the verified wall clock at read time is 08:40 COT, not 19:30. Two sessions never ran at all - 2026-08-20 endday and 2026-08-21 morning - and the 2026-08-21 midnight session fired LATE and CONCURRENTLY with this one, publishing at 08:45 COT with spot at 76,831.9, five minutes after this report was priced at 76,919.9. The last report available when this analysis was built was therefore 2026-08-20-midday at 12:50 COT with spot at 72,738.7, and the bias review below compares against THAT report. The concurrent midnight run is worth naming because it is an independent check rather than a repetition: it reached the same overall bias, the same bearish tilt, the same 6.0 confidence and the same TAKE_PROFIT stance from the same data, with slightly different trigger levels at 75,750.0 and 77,750.0. The gap this report has to bridge is not the usual six and a half hours - the next scheduled run is ~02:00 tomorrow, roughly seventeen hours away. THE MARKET: BTC has gone vertical. Spot is 76,919.9, up 7.78 percent on the rolling 24h and up 5.75 percent from the last report's 72,738.7. The 08:00Z hourly bar printed 79,515.7 and then gave back 3,293.5 points into a 76,222.2 low three hours later. The day's UTC range is 73,020.2 to 79,515.7, an 8.90 percent swing, and price is above all four daily EMAs including the EMA200 at 71,712.1 by 7.26 percent.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close below $76,222.2 - the low of the 13:00Z hourly bar, which is the deepest point of the give-back from 79,515.7. This is 697.7 points under spot and the 1H ATR is 1,024.3, so an ordinary hourly bar reaches it without meaning anything; that is exactly why the trigger is a settled CLOSE and not a touch. Losing it on a closing basis says the 79,515.7 spike was distribution rather than expansion, and it opens the 76,000 round number, then the 75,473.8 close of the 05:00Z bar and the 74,914.7 low that started the Bogota session. The liquidation tape argues the same way: 9,933,616 USD of the last four and a half hours of realized liquidations sit in the three 250-dollar bands immediately BELOW spot at 76,250, 76,500 and 76,750, and every dollar of the 76,250 and 76,500 bands is sell-side long liquidation. That is a market whose recent memory is longs being taken out at exactly this price.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close above $78,258.6 - the high of the 10:00Z hourly bar and the highest level price has held since the spike faded, 1,338.7 points overhead. Clearing it on a close would mean the give-back was a pause inside the leg rather than a top, and it would put the 79,270.3 close of the 08:00Z bar and then the 79,515.7 high back in play. Note what a break up here WOULD have that most breaks do not: measured fuel. There is 964,971 USD of buy-side short liquidation stacked at 78,250 and a further 133,664 at 78,000, so a push through that shelf has a genuine short book to run into. Note also what it would be doing: extending a move that already carries a 4H RSI of 89.0 and a daily RSI of 84.2. Buying that break is a momentum trade, not a value trade, and it should be sized as one.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from the last report's ADD to TAKE_PROFIT, and the reason is that the last report's thesis worked so well that it has stopped being a thesis and started being a risk. 2026-08-20-midday deployed 18.00 USDT of spot at 72,738.7 on a reclaim of the 29 May daily low at 72,508.0. Spot is 76,919.9. That tranche is up 5.75 percent in under twenty hours and the whole spot core is up 17.24 percent against a 65,606.6 average entry. Three things changed in a way that argues for banking part of it rather than pressing. FIRST, the extension is now historically stretched: price sits 7.26 percent above the daily EMA200, the 4H RSI is 89.0 and the daily RSI is 84.2, and the daily ATR has expanded to 2,124.7, so a single ordinary daily bar can now travel 2.76 percent. SECOND, the market already showed what it does up there - 79,515.7 was rejected for 3,293.5 points in three hours, and the fade produced 16,057,562 USD of long liquidations against only 2,208,906 USD of short, a 7.27-to-1 flush that is the mirror image of the short squeeze that carried the last leg. THIRD, and this is the honest counterweight, the underlying bid is real rather than mechanical: open interest has RISEN 5.39 percent to 2,324,596,823 USD while price rose 5.75 percent, so unlike yesterday's short-covering leg this one is being paid for with new positions, and the Farside tape shows a four-day inflow streak of 297.5, 189.3, 517.2 and 606.3 million dollars into the US spot ETFs. That is why this is a TAKE_PROFIT on a fraction and not an EXIT. The structural bull case is intact; the price is simply a bad place to be adding, and the run after this one is roughly seventeen hours away.

overnightRisk: The gap this report has to cover is unusually long and unusually stretched, and both halves of that sentence matter. LENGTH: the next scheduled report is ~02:00 COT tomorrow. Because 2026-08-20 endday and 2026-08-21 morning never ran and 2026-08-21 midnight fired late, no session was awake between 12:50 COT yesterday and 08:40 COT today - the 8.90 percent daily range that has happened since then happened with nobody watching. Assume the same can happen again. STRETCH: price is 7.26 percent above the daily EMA200 with a 4H RSI of 89.0, and the daily ATR of 2,124.7 means an ordinary bar now carries 2.76 percent. A single average down-day from here reaches 74,795. SPECIFIC CATALYSTS. (1) The US cash session opened forty minutes ago with equities soft - QQQ closed -0.72 percent and VOO -0.83 percent yesterday and both are only marginally green today - while BTC is up 7.78 percent. That divergence usually resolves toward equities, not away from them, and the resolution window is the New York afternoon, entirely inside this gap. (2) The Farside row for 21 August is still 0.0 and will fill after the US close, some hours into this gap. Four consecutive inflow days ending 606.3 million is a high bar; a miss or an outflow print is the single most likely trigger for a give-back, and it lands when liquidity is thinnest. (3) The liquidation geography is hostile in exactly one direction. Of 18,266,467 USD of realized liquidations in the last four and a half hours, 9,933,616 sit in the three bands directly below spot and are overwhelmingly long-side, so the path down has recent precedent and thin defence, while the only meaningful cluster above is 964,971 USD at 78,250. (4) Funding has flipped from a discount to a small premium - settled 0.0000807, current period 0.0001000, premium +0.000110 - so the perpetual is no longer paying you to be long the way it was at 72,738.7. THE PROTECTION. A resting stop is the only thing that works across a seventeen-hour gap, and the recommended level is 74,890.0, placed 20.7 points under the 74,914.7 low that started the Bogota session. That is 2,029.9 points below spot, roughly two 1H ATRs and just under one daily ATR, which is wide enough that ordinary overnight noise will not take it and tight enough that it exits before 73,031.7, the level at which the entire day is erased. Do not tighten it toward 76,222.2 overnight - that sits inside a single 1H ATR and inside the densest long-liquidation shelf on the tape, which is the precise definition of a stop that gets hunted.

liquidation.note: 5,473,195 USD across 220 fills and one hundred percent of it sell-side long liquidation - not a single buy-side fill in the band. This is the single heaviest cluster on the tape and it sits 419.9 points below spot. It is where the fade from 79,515.7 finally caught the longs that chased the spike. Magnet flag is on it because it is the heaviest measured band by a wide margin, 59 percent larger than the next one. Read it as memory rather than as resting orders - these are realized fills - but the geography is what matters for tonight: a market that just liquidated five and a half million dollars of longs at 76,500 has very little long-side defence left immediately under spot.

3,432,045 USD across 238 fills, split 3,240,523 sell-side against 191,522 buy-side. It sits 80.1 points ABOVE spot, which is to say the market is standing directly underneath it. The near-total sell-side skew tells you this band was worked on the way DOWN through 77,000 rather than on the way up, so the level has already been paid for once. Reclaiming it would not be a squeeze - the fuel is spent - it would have to be bought with real demand.

2,245,743 USD across 95 fills, again one hundred percent sell-side long liquidation. The deepest band of the flush, sitting at the 76,222.2 low of the 13:00Z bar. Combined with 76,500 and 76,750 this is 9,933,616 USD of long liquidation concentrated in a 500-point corridor immediately below spot, and it is the mechanical reason the reduce trigger is set at 76,222.2 rather than lower.

2,215,078 USD across 277 fills, 2,212,635 of it sell-side against 2,443 buy. The highest fill count of any band, which means it was worked repeatedly rather than in one flush - the market chopped across 76,750 several times during the give-back. It is 169.9 points below spot and it is the first shelf a failure would test.

1,623,762 USD across 176 fills, 1,453,879 sell-side against 169,883 buy. Overhead by 580.1 points. Like the 77,000 band this is predominantly long liquidation booked on the way down, so it marks where the give-back accelerated rather than where a short book is waiting.

1,447,155 USD across 266 fills and the most genuinely two-way band on the tape - 748,567 buy-side against 698,587 sell. It is 330.1 points overhead and it is the nearest cluster above spot. A two-way band is a pivot, not a wall: it says both books have been punished there and neither owns it.

964,971 USD across 133 fills and one hundred percent buy-side short liquidation. This is the ONLY band above spot that is clean short-side, and it sits at 78,250, essentially on top of the 78,258.6 add gate. That is not a coincidence: it is the shelf where shorts got run on the way to 79,515.7, and it is the only measured fuel a continuation has to work with.
730,854 USD across 153 fills, 729,836 of it sell-side. A thin long-liquidation band 830.1 points overhead, part of the same downward sequence as 78,000 and 77,500.

133,664 USD across 42 fills, 130,501 buy-side. The smallest band on the tape and the thinnest patch of the whole corridor between spot and the day's high. Its smallness is the point: between 78,000 and 79,515.7 the market barely transacted at all on the way down, so a move back up into that pocket would travel fast in either direction.

liquidityMagnet.note: Pull reads DOWN, and this time it is weight rather than an artefact of what has been measured. The window covers the whole spike and the whole give-back, so both sides of spot are genuinely sampled - unlike yesterday, when everything above price was simply untraded. Of 18,266,467 USD of realized liquidations, 16,057,562 are sell-side long liquidations and only 2,208,906 are buy-side short, a ratio of 7.27 to 1. Below spot sits 9,933,616 USD across three bands that are effectively pure long-side. Above spot sits 7,332,451 USD, but 6,124,255 of that is ALSO long liquidation booked on the way down through 77,000, 77,500 and 77,750 - spent fuel, not resting shorts. Strip it out and the only genuine short-side magnet overhead is 964,971 USD at 78,250 plus 130,501 at 78,000. The forward implication is uncomfortable and worth stating plainly: a failure of 76,222.2 travels into a corridor that has just been emptied of long-side support, while a break above 77,480.4 has roughly a million dollars of short fuel to work with and then nothing mapped until the high.

liquidations.note: 1,600 realized fills between 09:12:50Z and 13:36:28Z, the newest three minutes old at read time. Long liquidations of 16,057,562 USD against short liquidations of 2,208,906 - a 7.27-to-1 flush and the exact mirror image of the short squeeze that carried the previous leg. skew is the OKX long/short ACCOUNT ratio at the 13:00Z print, 1.10, and its path is the most useful thing on this line: it ran to 1.33 at the 08:00Z bar as accounts chased the spike, then fell to 1.17, 1.16, 1.05, 1.11 and 1.10 as the fade liquidated them. Crowding built and was destroyed inside five hours. Open interest is 2,324,596,823 USD, UP 5.39 percent against the 2,205,746,722 of the last report while price rose 5.75 percent. That near-proportionality is the strongest single argument for the bull case here: unlike yesterday's leg, which advanced on FALLING open interest and was therefore shorts leaving, this one is being paid for with new positions arriving. Funding cuts the other way - the settled rate is 0.0000807 and the current period is at the 0.0001000 base with a premium of +0.000110, so the perpetual has flipped from the discount it held at 72,738.7 to a small premium. Longs now pay to be long. That is not stress, but it is no longer a tailwind.

calibration.note: The prior report is 2026-08-20-midday, published at 12:50:00-05:00 with spot at 72,738.7. It graded well on both halves for the first time in three sessions. ANALYSIS: midday published a reduce line at 72,508.0 requiring a settled hourly close and an add gate at 73,185.0 on the same condition. The reduce line FIRED - the 18:00Z hourly bar settled 72,431.9, seventy-six point one points below it - so priorReduceFired is true. It fired shallowly and reverted within two bars, with the 20:00Z bar closing 72,667.1 and the 23:00Z bar closing 73,031.7. The add gate fired next, when the 00:00Z bar settled 73,714.3 and cleared 73,185.0 by 529.3 points, and price has not looked back since. Naming both edges and having the market trade the lower one first, reject it, and then clear the upper one is a correct reading of a coiled shelf. ACTION: midday deployed 18.00 USDT of spot at 72,738.7 and held 45.08 back. That tranche is worth 19.03 USDT at 76,919.9, up 5.75 percent, so actingHelped is true. The specific thing it got right was refusing to treat a rising long/short account ratio as a top signal in isolation - the lesson written after the 20 August morning trim - and instead pairing it with open interest and funding. The criticism, and it is real, is symmetrical to yesterday's: midday held 45.08 USDT back for a 72,508.0 retest or an endday ETF print, and neither the retest nor the endday session ever arrived. The cash sat idle through a 5.75 percent move because the scheduler dropped the 20 August endday and 21 August morning runs and fired midnight nineteen hours late. That is not an analytical error, but it is the second consecutive session where the withheld half was the half that mattered, and it argues for smaller reserves when the next scheduled run is more than a few hours away.
